result:
The answer 4 is consistent with what I recall of the known result, though I did not re-derive the regularity theorem and am relying partly on memory.

The upper bound is solid. For G = SU(2) = S³, which is an allowed group, the map x/|x| : B⁴ → S³ is energy minimizing (Schoen–Uhlenbeck). It is therefore stable and stationary, and its singular set is the single point at the origin, which has codimension exactly 4. So no guarantee better than 4 is possible.

The lower bound of 4 matches what I recall of the theorem for these groups. The cone over a totally geodesic 2-sphere is unstable, which is the kind of instability argument that rules out the codimension-3 case. The excluded groups (Sp(n) for n ≥ 8, E₈, F₄, G₂) are exactly where the instability argument is not available. This is the part I did not verify independently.

The proposed solution's sharpness argument is slightly loose in its wording about topological obstruction, but the conclusion is right.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
